summary: South Sudan's eVisa portal (evisa.gov.ss) says you apply, pay with a credit or debit card and download the e-visa online, then present it to the visa officer at the port of entry; the UK Foreign Office tells British nationals they must have a visa and can apply online or through the South Sudanese Embassy. No official visa fee is currently published. The UK, Canadian and Australian governments advise against all travel to South Sudan.

vaccinations.name: Malaria prophylaxis
vaccinations.text: Not an entry requirement. WHO's country list says malaria risk, predominantly P. falciparum, exists throughout the year in the entire country.

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for South Sudan. The UK Foreign Office says health facilities are extremely limited throughout the country and many medical problems need evacuation to Nairobi or Kampala, and advises adequate travel health insurance and accessible funds for treatment, evacuation and repatriation.

onwardTicket.text: No official source we could read states an onward- or return-ticket requirement for South Sudan.

declarations.name: Registration with the police
declarations.text: The UK Foreign Office says you must register at a local police station if you are in South Sudan for 5 days or more.

source.name: UK FCDO travel advice — South Sudan entry requirements

currencyLimits.text: No official source we could read states South Sudan's cash-declaration threshold. The UK Foreign Office says you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty, and to contact the South Sudanese Embassy for information.

notes: The UK Foreign Office says there are strict rules on goods you can take into or out of South Sudan, and you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.

Canada's travel advice says a permit from the Ministry of Information is required for photography, including on a mobile phone, and that even with one it is prohibited to photograph military installations, military and police personnel, government buildings and infrastructure such as roads, bridges, dams and airfields, and public utilities.

postArrivalRegistration.text: The UK government says you must register at a local police station if you are in South Sudan for 5 days or more.

payments.text: The UK Foreign Office says international credit and debit cards are not widely accepted, although some newer hotels and supermarkets are starting to, that ATMs are hard to find and often do not take international cards, and advises bringing large-denomination US dollars in clean, unblemished notes dated 2017 onwards.
